notes: The metro is safe and clean (Bilhete Único card); Uber and 99 are cheap; traffic is terrible (17:00-20:00). Guarulhos is 45-90 minutes away; Congonhas is inside the city.
June to September is the dry winter, 15-24°C (the most comfortable, cool at night); the Bixiga festival is in August; fog is possible.

SAFETY: in the Centre (Sé, Luz, 25 de Março) keep your wallet in front by day and avoid it when empty at night; don't take your phone out on the street. Paulista, Jardins and Vila Madalena are relaxed.
Pizza 80-100 BRL, per-kilo restaurant 50, mortadella sandwich 40, padaria breakfast 30; 10% service is included; Pix and cards are accepted everywhere.
MASP is free on Tuesdays and Pinacoteca on Saturdays; Paulista is pedestrian-only on Sundays; book A Casa do Porco months ahead; Embu is best at weekends.
Coxinha, pão de queijo (cheese bread), pastel, mortadella, feijoada (Wednesday and Saturday), caipirinha; Japanese food in Liberdade.

stops.name: MASP
stops.tips: Lina Bo Bardi's museum suspended in mid-air; Van Gogh and Portinari on glass easels. Free on Tuesdays, and Paulista is car-free on Sundays.

stops.name: Avenida Paulista
stops.tips: The financial boulevard; pedestrian-only on Sundays, with street musicians and Japan House.

stops.name: Bráz Pizzaria Paulista
stops.tips: São Paulo pizza (the city ranks as the world's second pizza city); thin crust, muçarela de búfala (buffalo mozzarella).

stops.name: Parque Trianon
stops.tips: A remnant of Atlantic forest on Paulista; welcome shade.

stops.name: Sesc Avenida Paulista Terası
stops.tips: A free rooftop terrace with a city panorama, inside a cultural centre.

backups.name: Mocotó Vila Medeiros
backups.tips: A legend of northeastern Brazilian cooking; far out but worth it (take an Uber).

backups.name: Instituto Moreira Salles
backups.tips: Photography museum with a terrace, on Paulista; free.

stops.name: Mercado Municipal Mercadão
stops.tips: A 1933 market with stained-glass windows; try the mortadella sandwich (Hocca Bar, 300 g) and pastel de bacalhau (salt cod pastry), and taste exotic fruit (the vendors are insistent).

stops.name: Catedral da Sé & Marco Zero
stops.tips: A neo-Gothic cathedral and the city's zero point; nearby is Pátio do Colégio (founded in 1554).

stops.name: Edifício Martinelli / Farol Santander
stops.tips: A 1929 skyscraper; Farol Santander has a viewing deck on the 26th floor and a skate ramp.

stops.name: Theatro Municipal
stops.tips: A copy of the Paris Opera; tours run Wednesday to Friday, on Praça Ramos de Azevedo.

stops.name: Edifício Copan
stops.tips: Niemeyer's wavy building with 1,160 apartments; see it from outside (the terrace may be closed), and try Bar da Dona Onça.

backups.name: Bar da Dona Onça Copan
backups.tips: Brazilian classics at the foot of the Copan; feijoada (black bean and pork stew) on Saturdays.

backups.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
backups.tips: A museum in a Ramos de Azevedo brick building; Brazilian art, free on Saturdays, next to Luz station.

stops.name: Parque Ibirapuera
stops.tips: The city's Central Park, with Niemeyer pavilions; bikes, a lake and the Oca.

stops.name: Museu Afro Brasil
stops.tips: African-Brazilian culture inside the park; slavery and art.

stops.name: Figueira Rubaiyat Jardins
stops.tips: Steak under a giant fig tree, in the upscale Jardins district.

stops.name: Rua Oscar Freire
stops.tips: Brazil's most luxurious street; the Havaianas flagship store and Melissa.

stops.name: Museu da Imagem e do Som
stops.tips: Museum of sound and image; pop exhibitions.

backups.name: A Casa do Porco
backups.tips: Among the world's 50 best restaurants; pork tasting menu, in the Centre. Book months ahead.

backups.name: Casa de Vidro Lina Bo Bardi
backups.tips: The architect's glass house in Morumbi; reservation required.

stops.name: Beco do Batman
stops.tips: Graffiti on Batman Alley in Vila Madalena; it changes every week.

stops.name: Coffee Lab Vila Madalena
stops.tips: A Brazilian coffee laboratory; run by Isabela Raposeiras.

stops.name: Mercado de Pinheiros
stops.tips: A neighbourhood market; Comedoria Gonzales serves Peruvian food by Rodrigo Oliveira.

stops.name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
stops.tips: Ruy Ohtake's purple-and-red building in Pinheiros; free exhibitions.

stops.name: Vila Madalena Bar Akşamı São Cristóvão
stops.tips: A football-fanatic bar on Rua Aspicuelta; street party on Fridays and Saturdays.

backups.name: Praça Benedito Calixto Pazarı
backups.tips: Saturday antiques and crafts market; choro music.

backups.name: Bar Veloso Vila Mariana
backups.tips: The city's best coxinha (chicken croquette) and caipirinha; expect a queue.

stops.name: Liberdade Japon Mahallesi
stops.tips: The largest Japanese community outside Japan; red torii gates and lanterns, plus the Praça da Liberdade market on Sundays.

stops.name: Liberdade Ramen Aska
stops.tips: A small Japanese ramen shop; queue, cash only.

stops.name: Museu da Imigração Mooca
stops.tips: A former immigrant hostel (like Ellis Island); Italian, Japanese and Turkish-Syrian migration.

stops.name: Bixiga Italyan Mahallesi
stops.tips: Cantinas on Rua 13 de Maio; the Vai-Vai samba school, and the Nossa Senhora Achiropita festival in August.

stops.name: Cantina Famiglia Mancini
stops.tips: A cantina on Rua Avanhandava dating from 1980; giant portions of pasta, and a queue.

backups.name: Templo Busshinji Liberdade
backups.tips: A Zen temple; an alternative to the museum.

backups.name: Sujinho Consolação
backups.tips: A late-night steakhouse; churrasco (grilled meat), open 24 hours.

stops.name: Embu das Artes Feira de Artesanato
stops.tips: A colonial artists' town 27 km away; crafts fair at weekends (shops only on weekdays), one hour by bus.

stops.name: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário Embu
stops.tips: A 1690 Jesuit church with a museum of sacred art.

stops.name: Restaurante Os Girassóis Embu
stops.tips: A restaurant in a colonial house; feijoada and Minas Gerais cooking.

stops.name: Embu Antikacılar & Rüstik Mobilya
stops.tips: Wooden furniture and ceramics; shipping available.

stops.name: Parque Villa-Lobos Dönüş
stops.tips: A park in western São Paulo; sunset and cycling.

backups.name: Parque Estadual da Cantareira
backups.tips: Atlantic forest north of the city; Pedra Grande viewpoint, nature instead of Embu.

stops.name: Parque Buenos Aires Higienópolis
stops.tips: A French-style garden; a neighbourhood morning.

stops.name: Padaria Santa Teresa
stops.tips: Breakfast at a padaria (Brazilian bakery); pão na chapa (grilled buttered bread) and pingado (coffee with milk), a farewell treat.

stops.name: Museu do Futebol Pacaembu
stops.tips: A football museum inside Pacaembu stadium; Pelé and Garrincha, interactive.

stops.name: Guarulhos Havalimanı Uber
stops.tips: 45-90 minutes by Uber depending on traffic; farewell.

backups.name: Museu do Ipiranga
backups.tips: The Independence Museum, restored in 2022; gardens, an alternative to football.
